tags: why do dogs lean on you
script: When your dog leans their full body weight against your leg, that's one of the clearest signs of trust and affection a dog can give. In the wild, physical closeness like that would leave an animal vulnerable, so choosing to lean their whole body onto you, essentially giving up their own balance and mobility, signals real comfort and security. Some behaviorists describe it as a self-soothing behavior too, similar to how a hug can be calming for a person, the pressure and contact can lower a dog's stress in the moment. It's especially common in dogs who are anxious in a new environment, using you as a stable, trusted anchor point. So that heavy lean against your leg isn't your dog being clingy or in the way. It's one of the most direct physical trust signals in their entire behavioral vocabulary.
